thread:
alex: FYI — support escalated a high-severity latency regression for AcmeCorp. p95 ~450ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~900ms -> 2.6s after the 2026-03-12 runtime roll.

maya: ouch. any obvious error rates or queueing?

support-bot: Ticket #INC-4281: Customer reports timeouts and slow responses for /v1/generate (model: redwood-qa-13b). No auth or billing issues. Logs attached.

alex: errors are mostly 504 and high tail token latency. No spike in 429. CPU usage ok, GPU utilting at ~60-70%. Observed longer kernel times on attention kernels per perf traces.

samir: that lines up with the kernel selector change we merged in 2026-03-12. We flipped default to select FlashAttention where supported, fallback to SDPA only as fallback. Could be kernel perf regression on longer sequences.

lina: do we have repro? can we run the same request shape locally with latest build?

alex: repro steps in ticket: prompt ~900 tokens, generation 256 tokens, top_p sampling, temperature 0.7. I can share curl.

alex: ```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-qa-13b","prompt":"<long prompt ~900 tokens>","max_tokens":256}'
```

maya: running that locally on a gpusim node now. tagging samir. @samir can you check kernel timings?

samir: running perf harness. initial run with runtime v2026-03-12 shows attention kernel time ~1.8ms per token step vs expected ~0.45ms. That's the regression.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: deployment v2026-03-12 finished. commit: b3f1a9.

lina: any compile-flag differences? we recently enabled avx512_fallback in the builder for some hosts.

samir: noted. The kernel selector picks FlashAttention path which expects certain warp/block sizes. On some GPUs (older Ampere variants) our FlashAttention has a pathological path for long sequences. SDPA was faster previously.

alex: customer is on dedicated GPUType: a100-sxm4-40. Should be fine though. But perf traces show the codepath hit divergent loads.

maya: quick mitigation — can we flip a runtime toggle to prefer SDPA for that model while we debug?

samir: yes. We have runtime flag `attention_kernel_preference` per model. Options: [auto, flash, sdpa]. Default is auto. I can set model override to sdpa for redwood-qa-13b in prod.

samir: doing it now... patching model config and rolling out to 3 pods for canary.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: model-config update applied to redwood-qa-13b (canary).

maya: canary metrics?

samir: canary p99 dropped back to ~420ms, p95 ~370ms. Looks promising.

alex: told support to route AcmeCorp to the canary pool (they're on dedicated, we can pin). Support confirmed reduced latency on their side.

support-bot: AcmeCorp confirms latency restored to expected levels, no more timeouts.

lina: good quick win. Next we need root cause: why FlashAttention regressed. Repro locally with debug kernels and symbols.

samir: I pulled flamegraphs. The expensive functions are nvptx kernels used by flash attention microkernels. The selector chose a variant optimized for short sequences but inefficient for long sequences; our heuristics rely on sequence length threshold which the recent selector tweak lowered. The compile flags also changed alignment assumptions (we enabled -ftree-vectorize and updated sm_version detection).

alex: so it's a combo: selector heuristics + compile flag behavior on some GPU SM versions.

maya: plan: 1) revert selector tweak (restore previous thresholds) 2) run full microbenchmark matrix across model sequence lengths 3) add e2e perf test in CI.

samir: agree. immediate step is to keep sdpa override for affected model families while we test. I'll open PR to revert the threshold change and add more fine-grained rules per GPU arch.

samir: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pull/891 (WIP) — includes a flag `kernel_selector.long_seq_threshold = 1024` and a test harness.

lina: also let's add runtime feature to expose a per-customer override until we have a permanent fix. Some customers run critical SLAs and we should be able to route them to the stable kernel.

alex: agreed. support asked for a short postmortem note to send to customer. I'll draft.

maya: ops note: for observability, we should emit 'kernel_variant' tag on traces and metrics (flash|sdpa|other) so we can slice p95/p99 by kernel.

samir: adding that to PR. Also adding micro-benchmarks for token lengths in 128/256/512/1024/2048 to CI.

lina: long-term: consider adding an adaptive runtime where if tail latency crosses threshold we fallback to sdpa for that session. Might be tricky but useful.

alex: customer comms: I posted draft: "We identified a kernel selection heuristic change in our March runtime rollout that caused suboptimal FlashAttention kernel selection for long inputs on some GPU types. We've temporarily routed you to the SDPA kernel and latency should be restored. We're rolling a code fix and will follow up with full test results." :thumbsup:

support-bot: Customer pinged: thanks for quick action. Please keep them posted.

maya: next steps checklist: 
- samir: revert selector heuristics + tests (ETA 24h)
- samir: land kernel variant tagging in metrics (ETA 48h)
- ops: keep model override in place (until fix)
- alex & support: customer follow-up and postmortem (ETA 48h)

samir: created issue RED-1247 for regression tracking and linked PRs.

alex: one more mitigation if we see recurrence — add runtime config to limit max_sequence for FlashAttention to 1024 and auto-fallback beyond that. Less ideal but safe.

lina: agreed. Also let's check our canary matrix to include long-prompt tests. They were missing. Adding them to the rollout checklist.

maya: thanks all. great triage. :eyes:

samir: will follow up with perf graphs and PR links in thread.

ops-bot: NOTE: rollback not required. Canary override in place.

alex: closing loop with customer once PR merges and we finish validation.
